analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent anogenital infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) types causes substantial disease burden in males, yet efficacy data for the 9-valent HPV (9vHPV) vaccine in this population were limited. The study addressed the knowledge gap regarding whether the 9vHPV vaccine prevents persistent infection in males aged 16–26 years.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial was conducted at 22 clinical sites in Japan. Healthy males aged 16–26 years with no prior HPV vaccination or HPV-related lesions were centrally randomised 1:1 to receive three intramuscular injections of 9vHPV vaccine or saline placebo at day 1, month 2, and month 6.
analysis.methods: The primary and secondary efficacy endpoints were the combined incidences of 6-month anogenital persistent infection related to HPV6, 11, 16, 18 and HPV31, 33, 45, 52, 58. Anogenital swabs and external genital tissue samples were tested for HPV DNA, with tissue samples adjudicated for histopathology. Superiority testing used a 0% margin in the per-protocol population. Immunogenicity was assessed at month 7 in the per-protocol immunogenicity population, and safety was evaluated in all participants receiving at least one dose.
analysis.main_results: Between Nov 30, 2020, and Dec 25, 2021, 1059 participants were enrolled (529 vaccine, 530 placebo). Vaccine efficacy for the primary endpoint was 89.3% (95% CI 55.4–98.2; p=0.0002) in the initial analysis and 91.6% (67.7–98.6) at study end. For the secondary endpoint, efficacy was 63.5% (2.7–86.0; p=0.023) initially and 72.9% (38.7–89.3) at study end. Seroconversion rates exceeded 98% for each vaccine-targeted HPV type.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that the 9vHPV vaccine prevents anogenital persistent infection related to vaccine-targeted HPV types in males and demonstrates an acceptable safety profile. This is the first efficacy trial of the 9vHPV vaccine in Japanese males aged 16–26 years, providing direct evidence of protection against multiple oncogenic and non-oncogenic HPV types.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the use of the 9vHPV vaccine in males to reduce HPV-related anogenital diseases, informing national immunisation policies and expanding vaccination recommendations to include adolescent and young adult males in Japan.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its short follow-up period and the exclusion of participants with prior HPV-related lesions or vaccination, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is moderate due to the single-country setting and reliance on surrogate endpoints rather than clinical disease outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This phase 3 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety of the 9-valent human papillomavirus (9vHPV) vaccine in 1059 healthy Japanese males aged 16–26 years. Participants received three intramuscular injections of 9vHPV vaccine or saline placebo at day 1, month 2, and month 6. The primary endpoint was the combined incidence of 6-month anogenital persistent infection with HPV6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, or 58. Vaccine efficacy against the primary endpoint was 89.3% (95% CI 55.4–98.2) in the initial analysis and 91.6% (67.7–98.6) at study end, with seroconversion rates exceeding 98% for each vaccine-targeted HPV type. Injection-site adverse events were more frequent in vaccine recipients (70%) than placebo (31%), though most were mild or moderate. No vaccine-related serious adverse events or deaths occurred. The authors interpret these results as demonstrating that the 9vHPV vaccine prevents anogenital persistent infection in males and has an acceptable safety profile, supporting its use to reduce HPV-related anogenital diseases in this population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Breast cancer is the most prevalent malignant tumor among women, and high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly HPV16, has been detected in breast tumors since the 1990s. Beyond its oncogenic potential, viral immune evasion in non-anogenital tumors such as oropharyngeal cancers underscores the need to investigate HPV activity in breast tissues.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 92 breast cancer patients were included after Ethics Committee approval, and clinical data were obtained from medical records. RNA was extracted from formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues and reverse-transcribed into cDNA for downstream analyses.
analysis.methods: Transcripts of HPV oncogenes (E5, E6, and E7), components of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, and regulatory genes (EGFR and PTEN) were quantified by RT-qPCR. Gene expression levels were calculated using the ΔCt method.
analysis.main_results: Forty-eight samples met RNA quality criteria and were included in the expression analysis. Among these, 77.08% showed expression of at least one viral oncogene, with E5 being the most frequently expressed. The PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway was modulated in HPV-positive samples, with increased PI3K expression and decreased mTOR expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The high expression of E5, associated with immune evasion, combined with reduced mTOR expression suggests that HPV16 status may influence therapeutic response in breast cancer patients. These findings reinforce the importance of further studies investigating HPV activity in breast tumors to better understand its biological and clinical impact.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights a potential role for HPV16 oncogene expression in modulating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway in breast cancer, which may inform future research on therapeutic resistance and immune evasion mechanisms in HPV-associated tumors.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its sample size and reliance on RNA extracted from formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues, which may affect RNA quality and quantification accuracy. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational design and lack of functional validation of the observed pathway modulation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the expression of HPV16 oncogenes E5, E6, and E7 in breast tumors and their association with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Among 92 breast cancer patients, 48 samples met RNA quality criteria, and 77.08% showed expression of at least one viral oncogene, with E5 being the most frequent. HPV-positive samples exhibited increased PI3K and decreased mTOR expression, suggesting a potential influence of HPV16 on therapeutic response via immune evasion mechanisms. The findings underscore the need for further research to clarify the biological and clinical impact of HPV activity in breast cancer.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate whether daily intravaginal silicon dioxide-based gel treatment increases the proportion of women with no detectable cervical high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) DNA compared with observation alone. Independent randomized evidence testing these short-term claims against observation is limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a prospective, single-center, parallel-group, randomized, open-label controlled trial involving 242 women with PCR-confirmed cervical hrHPV infection and no indication for immediate treatment. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive 3 months of self-administered daily intravaginal gel treatment or observation alone.
analysis.methods: The study used PCR to assess the absence of detectable cervical hrHPV DNA at 3 months. Secondary outcomes included patient-reported satisfaction and adverse events during the randomized study period.
analysis.main_results: At 3 months, hrHPV DNA was not detected in 18/99 women (18%) in the gel treatment group and 23/109 women (21%) in the observation group. Patient-reported adverse events were more frequent in the gel treatment group than in the observation group (32/99 [32%] vs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that 3 months of daily intravaginal silicon dioxide-based gel treatment did not improve short-term loss of detectable cervical hrHPV DNA compared with observation alone. The trial did not reproduce the large short-term virologic benefit suggested by prior product-related studies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that this intervention is not effective for promoting short-term hrHPV non-detectability in women without an indication for immediate treatment, particularly given the higher frequency of local adverse events.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had a relatively small sample size with primary-endpoint data available for 208 women, and a post hoc adjusted sensitivity analysis did not materially change the interpretation of the primary comparison. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effectiveness of a silicon dioxide-based vaginal gel in promoting short-term high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) clearance in women with cervical hrHPV infection. The study found no significant difference in hrHPV DNA detectability between the gel treatment group and the observation group at 3 months. Additionally, adverse events were more frequent in the gel treatment group. The authors concluded that the gel does not improve short-term hrHPV non-detectability and that the findings do not support its routine use for this purpose. The study's moderate evidence strength is due to its small sample size and the lack of significant results.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the prevalence and associated factors of HPV vaccination uptake among adolescent girls in Lesotho, as cervical cancer elimination requires reaching 90% vaccination coverage by age 15.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A population-based cross-sectional study was conducted among girls aged 15–17 in Lesotho, which reintroduced the national HPV vaccine programme in 2022.
analysis.methods: A multilevel Poisson regression model with robust variance was used to identify factors associated with HPV vaccination uptake, focusing on prevalence and its determinants.
analysis.main_results: The uptake of HPV vaccination among adolescent girls in Lesotho was 52.15% (95% CI 48.43 to 55.84).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that awareness about cervical cancer and STIs is linked to higher vaccination uptake, while older age and residence in Maseru district are associated with lower uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted education strategies to improve HPV vaccination rates, particularly in districts with low uptake, and emphasize the importance of awareness campaigns for cervical cancer prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the evidence is moderate due to potential biases in self-reported data.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study examines HPV vaccination uptake among adolescent girls in Lesotho, a country that reintroduced its national HPV vaccine programme in 2022. The study found that 52.15% of girls aged 15–17 had received the vaccine, with significant associations between vaccination uptake and factors such as age, district of residence, and awareness of cervical cancer and STIs. The authors emphasize the need for targeted education to improve uptake, particularly in areas with lower rates. The study's findings are relevant for public health strategies aiming to meet WHO targets for cervical cancer elimination. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to infer causality, and the evidence is considered moderate due to potential biases in self-reported data.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess parents’ knowledge and perceptions regarding HPV vaccination and identify factors associated with poor knowledge among parents of girls aged 12–18 years in Tunisia. Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a highly effective strategy for preventing cervical cancer and other HPV-related diseases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A quantitative, descriptive, cross-sectional, and analytical study was conducted among parents of girls aged 12–18 years in Sfax, Tunisia. Among 350 participants, the median age was 35 years, and 302 (86.3%) were mothers.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using an anonymous self-administered questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of HPV infection and vaccination, and perceptions toward HPV vaccination. Factors associated with poor knowledge were analyzed.
analysis.main_results: Although 238 (68.0%) parents had heard of HPV and 262 (74.9%) had heard of HPV vaccination, knowledge remained limited, with a median score of 2 (IQR: 1–3); 139 (39.7%) participants had poor knowledge. Only 16 (4.6%) reported that their child had received HPV vaccination, whereas 167 (47.7%) refused it.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Lower education, low socioeconomic status, rural residence, unemployment, lack of previous HPV awareness, and absence of social media use were associated with poor knowledge. Despite relatively high HPV awareness, parental knowledge and vaccine uptake remain insufficient in Tunisia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Targeted education by healthcare professionals, school-based awareness programs, and evidence-based communication strategies are needed to improve HPV vaccine acceptance. The findings can inform public health initiatives aimed at increasing HPV vaccination rates among parents of adolescent girls in Tunisia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to data collected from a single city in Tunisia, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is based on self-reported data, which may introduce bias. The confidence is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated parental knowledge and perceptions regarding HPV vaccination for cervical cancer prevention in Tunisia. It found that while awareness of HPV and its vaccine was relatively high, knowledge levels remained limited, with a median score of 2 (IQR: 1–3). Only 4.6% of parents reported their child had received the vaccine, and 47.7% refused it. Key barriers included concerns about side effects and insufficient information. Lower education, low socioeconomic status, rural residence, unemployment, and lack of social media use were linked to poor knowledge. The study highlights the need for targeted education and awareness programs to improve vaccine acceptance. However, the findings are based on self-reported data from a single city, limiting generalisability and introducing potential bias.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the relationship between molecular interactions and the mechanical properties of viral capsids, specifically addressing the lack of quantitative data linking atomistic interactions to macroscopic elastic parameters in HPV-16.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed an atomistic framework to investigate human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV-16) using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with umbrella sampling to evaluate the potential of mean force governing angular deviations between neighboring L1 pentamers.
analysis.methods: The researchers used all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with umbrella sampling to assess the potential of mean force and extract the preferred interaction angle and bending modulus between neighboring L1 pentamers in HPV-16.
analysis.main_results: The study found a clear decoupling between the spontaneous curvature of the HPV-16 capsid and its bending rigidity, with the bending modulus being an order of magnitude larger than previous estimates and strongly influenced by the electrostatic environment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that inter-capsomer rigidity is a key determinant of capsid size and shape, offering a quantitative framework for understanding how specific protein–protein interactions influence the mechanical properties of self-assembled viral capsids.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the mechanical behavior of HPV-16 capsids, which could inform the development of more effective diagnostic tools, therapeutic strategies, and vaccine design for HPV-associated diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an atomistic framework and does not include experimental validation, but the evidence is strong due to the detailed computational analysis and clear results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between molecular interactions and the mechanical properties of HPV-16 capsids, focusing on the bending modulus and preferred interaction angle between L1 pentamers. Using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with umbrella sampling, the researchers found a clear decoupling between spontaneous curvature and bending rigidity, with the bending modulus being significantly larger than previous estimates. The results highlight the importance of inter-capsomer rigidity in determining capsid size and shape, offering a quantitative framework for understanding how protein–protein interactions influence the mechanical properties of self-assembled viral capsids. These findings could have implications for the development of diagnostic tools, therapeutic strategies, and vaccine design for HPV-associated diseases. The study is limited to an atomistic framework without experimental validation, but the computational methods and results are robust and well-supported.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Female sex workers (FSW) have multiple sexual partners and are at higher risk of human papillomavirus virus (HPV) infection. They could be a target group for HPV vaccination, but their expected immune response to the HPV vaccine is unclear due to potential exposure to the virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a pilot study (NCT04590521) in Hai Phong, Vietnam to evaluate HPV vaccine immunogenicity among FSW aged 18-26 years. A total of 63 FSW with a median age of 23.4 years (IQR, 21.6-25.4 years) were recruited.
analysis.methods: All participants received the standard 3-dose schedule (0, 2, and 6 months) of the quadrivalent Gardasil vaccine (4vHPV). Blood samples were collected at baseline and at 2, 3, 6, and 7 months after the first dose to determine neutralizing antibody (nAb) responses to HPV16 and HPV18, as well as related HPV52 and HPV58.
analysis.main_results: Prevalence of any high-risk HPV type and HPV16/18 infection at baseline was 28.6% (18/63) and 9.5% (6/63), respectively. Following the first dose, 90% and 55% of individuals were seropositive for HPV16 and HPV18, respectively. By month 7, all participants were seropositive to both HPV16 and HPV18.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Three doses of 4vHPV elicited robust nAb to HPV16 and HPV18 among FSW. Higher nAb responses were observed among HPV-DNA-negative participants at baseline compared with HPV-DNA-positive participants after 2 and 3 doses (HPV16, geometric mean ratio [GMR] 2.97 and 1.63, P < .05; HPV18, GMR 2.83 and 1.49, P = .06).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HPV vaccination may be effective in FSW, who are at higher risk of HPV infection. This could inform targeted vaccination strategies for this high-risk group.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Further studies are needed to evaluate the effectiveness of HPV vaccination in FSW. The study was a pilot study with a limited sample size, which may affect the generalisability of the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity of the quadrivalent HPV vaccine (Gardasil) among female sex workers (FSW) in Vietnam. The research aimed to address the lack of understanding regarding immune responses in this high-risk group. A total of 63 FSW aged 18-26 years received the standard 3-dose schedule. Blood samples were collected to measure neutralizing antibody (nAb) responses to HPV16, HPV18, and related HPV52 and HPV58. At baseline, 28.6% of participants had any high-risk HPV infection, and 9.5% had HPV16/18. Following the first dose, 90% and 55% were seropositive for HPV16 and HPV18, respectively, with all participants seropositive by month 7. Higher nAb responses were observed in HPV-DNA-negative individuals compared to those positive at baseline. The authors concluded that the vaccine elicited robust nAb responses in FSW, suggesting potential effectiveness. However, the study was a pilot with a limited sample size, highlighting the need for further research to assess vaccine effectiveness in this population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer, primarily caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, is commonly detected using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based assays. However, these methods are time-consuming and require specialized instrumentation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay as a rapid alternative for HPV detection compared with conventional PCR testing. This study included 933 nonpregnant women aged ≥19 years who underwent HPV testing for cervical cancer screening or follow-up.
analysis.methods: The HPV panel included 14 high-risk types (16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68). Cervical swab samples underwent nucleic acid extraction followed by LAMP amplification using type-specific primers. Reactions were performed at 63 °C for 35 minutes, and results were interpreted colorimetrically (blue for positive, purple for negative).
analysis.main_results: Compared with PCR, the LAMP assay showed a sensitivity of 97.8% (95% CI: 94.4–100.0) for HPV types 16 and 18 and 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8–100.0) for the remaining high-risk types. Specificity across all types was 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8–100.0). The overall diagnostic accuracy was 99.5% (95% CI: 99.0–100.0).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The LAMP assay provides a rapid, simple, and accurate method for HPV detection and may serve as a useful point-of-care screening tool, particularly in resource-limited settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the LAMP assay could be a valuable tool for cervical cancer screening, especially in settings where PCR-based methods are not readily available.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single center and may not be generalizable to other populations. The evidence is strong, with high sensitivity and specificity reported for the LAMP assay compared to PCR.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the diagnostic performance of the colorimetric LAMP assay with conventional PCR for detecting high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) types in cervical cancer screening. The LAMP assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for HPV types 16, 18, and other high-risk types, with overall diagnostic accuracy of 99.5%. The authors suggest that the LAMP assay could serve as a rapid, simple, and accurate point-of-care screening tool, particularly in resource-limited settings. The study was conducted in a single center with 933 nonpregnant women aged ≥19 years. The results indicate that the LAMP assay is a promising alternative to PCR for HPV detection. However, the study's limited generalizability and single-center design may affect the confidence in its findings. The evidence supports a high confidence in the assay's performance for the target HPV types.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether host factors Secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor (SLPI) and Annexin A2 (AnxA2) modulate human papillomavirus (HPV) presence in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) from non-endemic regions, where HPV DNA has been detected despite classical association with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study retrospectively analyzed 44 histopathological confirmed NPC cases from non-endemic German regions using formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue samples.
analysis.methods: Nucleic acids were extracted from FFPE tissue, with DNA used for PCR-based detection of HPV and EBV, RNA for RT-PCR detection of HPV transcriptional activity, and RT-qPCR for quantification of SLPI and AnxA2 expression. Associations between viral status, host factor expression, and clinicopathological parameters were assessed using Fisher's exact test, Student's t-test, and one-way ANOVA.
analysis.main_results: EBV was detected in 65.9% of cases and HPV DNA in 29.6%, with all HPV-positive cases harboring HPV16 DNA; none expressed HPV16 RNA. HPV presence was associated with significantly lower SLPI and higher AnxA2 expression, while EBV status showed no effect on SLPI and was associated with lower AnxA2 levels.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that SLPI and AnxA2 expression defines a host microenvironment permissive for HPV DNA presence in NPC from non-endemic regions, whereas EBV status appears independent of these factors, highlighting a novel host-virus interaction specific to HPV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that host factors SLPI and AnxA2 may influence HPV entry into epithelial cells in NPC, potentially informing future surveillance or therapeutic strategies targeting these factors in HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, small sample size, and lack of HPV RNA expression, which restricts conclusions to HPV presence rather than active infection, warranting cautious interpretation and larger prospective studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether host factors Secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor (SLPI) and Annexin A2 (AnxA2) modulate human papillomavirus (HPV) presence in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) from non-endemic regions, where HPV DNA has been detected despite classical association with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). Retrospectively analyzing 44 NPC cases from Germany, the authors found EBV in 65.9% and HPV DNA in 29.6% of cases, with all HPV-positive cases harboring HPV16 DNA but no detectable HPV RNA. HPV presence correlated with significantly lower SLPI and higher AnxA2 expression, while EBV status showed no effect on SLPI and was associated with lower AnxA2 levels. The authors concluded that SLPI and AnxA2 expression defines a host microenvironment permissive for HPV DNA presence, independent of EBV status. These findings suggest a novel host-virus interaction specific to HPV in NPC, potentially informing future surveillance or therapeutic strategies targeting these factors in HPV-associated cancers. However, the retrospective design, small sample size, and absence of HPV RNA expression limit conclusions to HPV presence rather than active infection, warranting cautious interpretation and larger prospective studies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health need to understand whether adolescents receive the HPV vaccine alongside other routinely recommended adolescent vaccines during the same medical visit, reflecting concerns about missed opportunities for simultaneous vaccination.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The analysis used data from the 2023 National Immunization Survey-Teen (NIS-Teen) to examine vaccination timing among adolescents aged 13–17 years in the United States.
analysis.methods: Provider-reported vaccination histories were used to assess the timing of HPV vaccine receipt relative to tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis vaccine (Tdap), quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine (MenACWY), and influenza vaccine.
analysis.main_results: In 2023, 69.5% of adolescents aged 13–17 years received HPV vaccine with one or more other recommended vaccines in a single medical visit, and 47.8% received HPV vaccine, Tdap, and MenACWY together.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that HPV vaccination is commonly administered with other adolescent vaccines in a single visit, highlighting flexibility in schedule adherence across settings and family preferences.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform vaccination program planning by showing that simultaneous administration is feasible and widely practiced, supporting strategies to optimize coverage without compromising schedule adherence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to provider-reported survey data and does not capture clinical outcomes or reasons for non-simultaneous vaccination, warranting cautious interpretation of the observed patterns.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed 2023 NIS-Teen data to quantify how often adolescents aged 13–17 years in the United States receive HPV vaccine together with other recommended vaccines during a single medical visit. Among 69.5% of adolescents, HPV vaccination occurred alongside at least one other vaccine, and 47.8% received HPV, Tdap, and MenACWY together. The authors interpret these patterns as evidence that simultaneous vaccination is common and compatible with schedule flexibility across clinical settings and family preferences. The findings suggest that current adolescent vaccination programs can leverage simultaneous administration to improve coverage without compromising adherence to recommended schedules.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a leading cause of anogenital, cervical, and oropharyngeal cancers, with rising incidence of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) globally. The study aimed to assess public awareness and knowledge gaps regarding HPV and its link to OPC among adults in Makkah, Saudi Arabia.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among adults aged 18 years and older in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, with a sample size of 420 participants. Data were collected using structured, self-administered online questionnaires.
analysis.methods: The survey instrument captured sociodemographic data and assessed awareness and knowledge of HPV infection and its association with OPC. Descriptive statistics were applied, and multiple-choice questions used 'Yes', 'No', and 'Do not know' response options.
analysis.main_results: Among 420 participants, 51.7% had heard of HPV, 21.4% had encountered an HPV or OPC awareness campaign, and 88.1% reported insufficient knowledge about HPV and OPC. Only 43.1% recognized HPV as contagious, 44.3% knew it could be sexually transmitted, and 42.4% were aware of HPV vaccine availability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating substantial knowledge gaps about HPV transmission, prevention, and OPC risk among adults in Makkah. The novelty lies in quantifying these gaps within a Saudi Arabian population using a structured survey.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted educational interventions and public awareness campaigns to improve understanding of HPV transmission, vaccination, and OPC prevention in Makkah. Social media is identified as a preferred platform for delivering such education.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported online questionnaires limit causal inference and may introduce response bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to the non-random sampling and potential selection bias in an online survey.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, assessed public awareness and knowledge of human papillomavirus (HPV) and its association with oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) among 420 adults. The survey revealed significant knowledge gaps: only half had heard of HPV, fewer recognized its contagiousness or sexual transmission, and less than half were aware of HPV vaccine availability. Most participants (88.1%) reported insufficient knowledge and expressed a need for more information, with social media as the preferred awareness channel. The authors conclude that targeted educational interventions are urgently needed to improve HPV literacy and OPC prevention in the region.

analysis.research_question_and_background: HPV16 is a major etiological agent of cervical and other epithelial cancers, yet the mechanisms underlying host–pathogen interactions remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the responses of human peripheral blood leukocytes to engineered HPV16 L1/L2 chimeric virus-like particles (VLPs).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved experimental assays to characterize leukocyte engagement with HPV16 L1/L2 chimeric VLPs, produced in suspension by HEK 293-F cells. These VLPs were designed to mimic native viral structures while incorporating chimeric features that enhance stability and immunogenicity. The study focused on human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, including lymphocytes and monocytes, but not polymorphonuclear cells.
analysis.methods: The study used leukocyte phenotyping, VLP internalization, confocal colocalization, and endocytic pathway analyses to characterize interactions. Uptake was assessed via blockage assays using chlorpromazine, rCTB, filipin, nystatin, liquemine, and sodium azide to confirm CD71 transferrin receptor-mediated and other endocytic pathways.
analysis.main_results: Recombinant L1/L2 proteins assembled into structured VLPs were shown to interact with mononuclear cells, including lymphocytes and monocytes, but not with polymorphonuclear cells such as neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils. Uptake occurred via the CD71 transferrin receptor-mediated pathway, as well as other endocytic routes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that HPV16 L1/L2 chimeric VLPs interact with and are internalized by human peripheral blood mononuclear cells through CD71-associated and other endocytic pathways. This provides new insights into HPV16 VLP–leukocyte interactions and contributes to understanding the cellular mechanisms involved in VLP uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform future studies on HPV biology and VLP-based vaccine development, particularly in understanding how these particles interact with and are taken up by immune cells.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to experimental assays and does not include clinical or epidemiological data. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on in vitro analyses and does not extend to in vivo or human clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the interactions of HPV16 L1/L2 chimeric virus-like particles (VLPs) with human peripheral blood leukocytes. The research aimed to understand how these engineered VLPs are internalized by immune cells, focusing on mononuclear cells such as lymphocytes and monocytes, while excluding polymorphonuclear cells. The methods included leukocyte phenotyping, VLP internalization, confocal colocalization, and endocytic pathway analyses. Results showed that the VLPs interact with mononuclear cells and are internalized via the CD71 transferrin receptor-mediated pathway and other endocytic routes. The findings provide new insights into HPV16 VLP–leukocyte interactions and their cellular uptake mechanisms, which may be relevant for vaccine development. However, the study is limited to in vitro experimental assays, and the evidence is moderate due to the absence of clinical or epidemiological data.

analysis.research_question_and_background: HPV is increasingly implicated in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas, a disease relevant to dental practice, yet gaps persist in adolescents' knowledge about HPV and its oncogenic risks. The study aimed to evaluate knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding STIs, HPV, and HPV-related oropharyngeal cancer among Italian secondary-school students.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,224 secondary-school students in Apulia, Italy, at the end of the 2025/2026 school year using a self-administered 108-item questionnaire.
analysis.methods: A 63-item composite knowledge score was computed with “don’t know” answers scored as incorrect and adequate knowledge defined as ≥60% (Bloom’s cut-off). The minimum required sample size of 737 was calculated using Cochran’s formula adjusted for a cluster-sampling design effect.
analysis.main_results: Overall knowledge was low (mean 28.5%, SD 18.2), with only 5% reaching the ≥60% threshold. Only 14.8% of students were aware that HPV can cause oropharyngeal cancer, significantly lower in boys (11.2%) than girls (17.3%; p = 0.003). Knowledge was independently associated with female sex, age, and sexual experience.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating a critical knowledge gap about HPV and its oropharyngeal cancer risk, particularly among boys who face higher disease risk. They highlight the potential role of dental professionals in addressing this gap through education and prevention strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that school-based and clinical HPV-prevention strategies could benefit from integrating oral-health professionals to improve awareness and vaccination uptake among adolescents.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the reliance on self-reported data may introduce bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to the large sample size but constrained by the abstract-only scope and lack of detailed statistical reporting.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding sexually transmitted infections, HPV, and HPV-related oropharyngeal cancer among 1,224 Italian secondary-school students. Using a 108-item questionnaire, the authors found critically low HPV knowledge (mean 28.5%), with only 5% meeting an adequate knowledge threshold (≥60%). Awareness that HPV causes oropharyngeal cancer was particularly low (14.8%), especially among boys (11.2% vs. 17.3% in girls; p = 0.003). Knowledge correlated with female sex, older age, and sexual experience. Despite poor knowledge, 61.2% expressed willingness to receive the HPV vaccine. The authors propose leveraging dental visits to address HPV-related cancer prevention gaps, emphasizing the role of oral-health professionals in school-based and clinical HPV-prevention strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: Emerging epidemiological evidence indicates that persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes is independently associated with elevated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, challenging traditional paradigms of cardiovascular risk assessment.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review synthesises current observational data on this association, explores the potential inflammatory, immune, and metabolic mechanisms that may connect HPV to atherogenesis, and evaluates the emerging evidence for cardiovascular protection conferred by HPV vaccination.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Large cohort studies report significantly elevated risks of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular mortality among women with high-risk HPV infection, independent of conventional risk factors.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Despite these intriguing signals, the bulk of evidence is derived from cross-sectional and retrospective designs, and the direct demonstration of a causal link remains absent.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: We discuss critical methodological challenges—including confounding by sexual behaviour, socioeconomic status, and co-infections—and outline a roadmap for prospective cohort studies, mechanistic investigations, and rigorous risk-stratification research.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (CVD), highlighting epidemiological evidence linking persistent high-risk HPV infection to increased CVD risk. The review evaluates observational data, potential molecular mechanisms, and the role of HPV vaccination in cardiovascular protection. While large cohort studies show elevated risks of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular mortality among women with high-risk HPV, the evidence is largely observational, and causal links remain unproven. The review identifies methodological challenges, including confounding by sexual behavior, socioeconomic status, and co-infections, and proposes future research directions such as prospective studies and mechanistic investigations. Clarifying the HPV-CVD relationship could lead to novel prevention strategies through vaccination.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the association between HPV vaccination status and cervical cytological findings, HPV prevalence, and genotype distribution among Iranian women, providing real-world evidence from a population with limited epidemiological data.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted from March 2023 to February 2024 among 216 women aged 30–65 years attending a tertiary gynecology clinic in Babol, Iran. Participants underwent liquid-based cytology and HPV DNA genotyping.
analysis.methods: Demographic and clinical data were collected using structured questionnaires and medical records. Comparisons between vaccinated and unvaccinated women were performed using appropriate statistical tests.
analysis.main_results: Overall HPV prevalence was 39.8%. HPV infection was less frequent among vaccinated women (33.3%) than unvaccinated women (42.9%), although the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.18). The distribution of high-risk HPV genotypes differed significantly between vaccinated and unvaccinated participants (P < 0.001), with non-vaccine high-risk genotypes predominating among HPV-positive vaccinated women.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings provide novel epidemiological data on HPV genotype distribution among vaccinated and unvaccinated Iranian women and may help inform future HPV prevention strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the continued importance of cervical cancer screening alongside HPV vaccination, as non-vaccine high-risk HPV types remained common among vaccinated women.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the lack of statistical significance in HPV infection rates between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups, suggesting moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study examined the association between HPV vaccination status and cervical cytological findings, HPV prevalence, and genotype distribution among 216 Iranian women aged 30–65 years. The study found that HPV infection was less frequent in vaccinated women, but the difference was not statistically significant. The distribution of high-risk HPV genotypes differed significantly between vaccinated and unvaccinated participants, with non-vaccine high-risk genotypes predominating among HPV-positive vaccinated women. These findings provide novel epidemiological data on HPV genotype distribution in this population and highlight the continued importance of cervical cancer screening alongside HPV vaccination. The study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the lack of statistical significance in infection rates suggests moderate evidence strength.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the phenotypic spectrum of LIG4 syndrome, a rare immunodeficiency caused by biallelic LIG4 variants, focusing on its association with extensive cutaneous viral warts and multi-type HPV infection. The rationale stems from the need to expand clinical understanding of genotype-phenotype correlations in LIG4 syndrome beyond classical severe combined immunodeficiency presentations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a single-patient case report describing an 18-year-old male with compound heterozygous LIG4 variants presenting with extensive cutaneous viral warts and combined immunodeficiency. The proband exhibited systemic manifestations including short stature, chronic malnutrition, recurrent pulmonary infections, and chronic diarrhea.
analysis.methods: The study identified compound heterozygous LIG4 variants (c.833G > T; p.Arg278Leu and c.833G > A; p.Arg278His) via genetic sequencing. Immunophenotyping assessed lymphocyte subsets, and HPV typing detected both α-HPV and β-HPV in cutaneous lesions.
analysis.main_results: Immunophenotyping revealed panhypogammaglobulinemia, absent B cells, reduced T and NK cells, and nearly undetectable naïve T cells. Both α-HPV and β-HPV were detected in the cutaneous lesions. Compound heterozygous LIG4 variants at the same codon (c.833G) were confirmed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as an expansion of the phenotypic spectrum of LIG4 syndrome, highlighting rare presentations with extensive viral warts and combined lymphopenia. The novelty lies in documenting multi-type HPV infection in this immunodeficiency syndrome.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that clinicians should consider LIG4 syndrome in patients with unexplained combined immunodeficiency and extensive cutaneous viral warts, enabling earlier diagnosis and tailored management. The report also underscores the importance of HPV screening in such patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single case report, restricting generalizability and causal inference. The strength of evidence is low due to the absence of controls, longitudinal data, or mechanistic validation.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes an 18-year-old male with LIG4 syndrome caused by compound heterozygous LIG4 variants (c.833G > T and c.833G > A) presenting with extensive cutaneous viral warts and combined immunodeficiency. Immunophenotyping revealed panhypogammaglobulinemia, absent B cells, and reduced T and NK cells. Both α-HPV and β-HPV were detected in the lesions, expanding the known phenotypic spectrum of LIG4 syndrome. The study highlights the need for clinicians to consider LIG4 syndrome in patients with unexplained immunodeficiency and viral warts, enabling earlier diagnosis. However, the evidence is limited to a single case, precluding broader generalizations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the clinical significance of vulvar condyloma as a potential indicator of concurrent high-risk cervical HPV infection and abnormal cervical cytology, given that HPV is the principal cause of cervical cancer and precursor lesions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective observational study enrolled 407 women evaluated at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Izmir City Hospital, between January 2025 and January 2026, and categorized them by the presence or absence of histopathologically confirmed vulvar condyloma.
analysis.methods: Patients underwent cervical cytology, HPV testing, vulvar examination, and colposcopic biopsy when clinically indicated, with logistic regression analyses used to identify factors associated with vulvar condyloma.
analysis.main_results: Vulvar condyloma was identified in 180 patients (44.2%), abnormal cervical cytology in 66/180 (36.7%) with condyloma versus 41/227 (18.1%) without (p < 0.001), and high-risk HPV positivity in 104/180 (57.8%) versus 86/227 (37.9%) (p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that vulvar condyloma was independently associated with abnormal cervical cytology and high-risk HPV infection, particularly HPV16/18, suggesting it may serve as a clinically visible marker of concurrent cervical HPV-related disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support careful cervical evaluation in women presenting with vulvar condyloma to detect potential high-risk HPV infection and related cervical abnormalities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design and reliance on a single-center cohort limit generalisability, and CIN2+ associations should be interpreted cautiously until confirmed in larger prospective cohorts with standardized histopathological verification.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study of 407 women evaluated the association between vulvar condyloma and cervical HPV-related disease. Vulvar condyloma was present in 44.2% of participants and was significantly associated with abnormal cervical cytology (36.7% vs 18.1%, p < 0.001) and high-risk HPV positivity (57.8% vs 37.9%, p < 0.001), particularly HPV16 and HPV18. Multivariate analysis confirmed independent associations with adjusted odds ratios of 2.30 for HPV16 and 3.29 for HPV18. The authors propose that vulvar condyloma may serve as a clinically visible marker of concurrent cervical HPV-related disease, warranting thorough cervical evaluation in affected women. However, the single-center, retrospective design and limited biopsy confirmation constrain generalisability, and larger prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer is a serious disease that kills many women around the world, especially in developing countries. It is mostly caused by the Human Papillomavirus (HPV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among healthcare personnel in tertiary care hospitals in Lahore, Pakistan. A total of 200 healthcare personnel (61% medical officers and 39% nurses) took part from Fatima Memorial Hospital, Lahore.
analysis.methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study using an adapted questionnaire, having 3 portions of questions, knowledge questions, attitude questions, and practice questions. The data was collected from December 2025 to May 2026, and analyzed using Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) 26 Mean and Standard.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that most healthcare workers (73% n=146) have a good knowledge level. For example, 78% knew that HPV causes cervical cancer, 69% knew the vaccine is available in Pakistan, and 77% knew the correct age for the vaccine is 9–14 years. Also, 61% correctly chose the Pap smear as the screening test.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: However, there were some problems: about half of the participants did not know the correct guidelines for catch-up vaccination. Additionally, results also show a significant association between attitude and practice regarding HPV vaccination.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted training programs for healthcare workers to improve their knowledge and practices regarding HPV vaccination, which is crucial for cervical cancer prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single tertiary care hospital in Lahore, Pakistan, which may affect the generalisability of the findings. The evidence is moderate as it is based on self-reported data and a cross-sectional design.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitude, and practices of doctors and nurses regarding the HPV vaccine in tertiary care hospitals in Lahore, Pakistan. A cross-sectional survey using an adapted questionnaire was conducted among 200 healthcare workers from Fatima Memorial Hospital between December 2025 and May 2026. The results indicated that most participants had good knowledge about HPV and its vaccine, with 73% demonstrating a good understanding. However, about half were unaware of the correct guidelines for catch-up vaccination. The study also found a significant association between attitude and practice regarding HPV vaccination. These findings highlight the need for improved training programs to address knowledge gaps and enhance the confidence of healthcare workers in recommending the vaccine. The study's evidence is moderate due to its cross-sectional design and limited scope to a single hospital.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health need to optimize human papillomavirus (HPV) immunization schedules to increase global coverage and reduce costs by shifting from the standard three-dose regimen to reduced-dose schedules. It asked whether one-dose or two-dose schedules maintain adequate immunogenicity, efficacy, and safety compared with the three-dose schedule.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted, synthesizing data from PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, CNKI, and Wanfang Data up to February 15, 2026. Included trials evaluated different dose schedules of HPV vaccines in females aged 9–26 years.
analysis.methods: Two reviewers independently searched multiple databases and constructed a Bayesian random-effects model using the multinma package in R. Treatments were ranked with Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking (SUCRA) values, and primary outcomes were HPV-16/18 seroconversion rates and 6-month persistent infection.
analysis.main_results: For immunogenicity, the 9-valent three-dose regimen showed the highest seroconversion rate versus placebo (OR 62.45, 95% CrI 15.20–158.30; SUCRA 0.96), though estimates were driven by near-zero events in placebo arms. Single-dose schedules maintained clinically significant protection against persistent infection (e.g., 2-valent one-dose vs. placebo: OR 0.32, 95% CrI 0.07–0.96; SUCRA 0.61). Safety rankings indicated one-dose schedules had the lowest risk of injection-site pain.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that reduced-dose schedules induce lower antibody titers than the standard three-dose regimen but provide robust protective efficacy against persistent HPV infection with a superior safety profile. They highlighted that two-dose schedules in adolescents aged 9–14 years may be comparable to the three-dose regimen.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support adopting two-dose schedules in adolescents and suggest that a single-dose strategy could be a viable alternative in resource-constrained settings to accelerate cervical cancer elimination. The results imply that policy changes toward reduced-dose regimens may enhance vaccination coverage without compromising protection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the surrogate nature of endpoints and the constraints of network meta-analysis for establishing non-inferiority, warranting cautious interpretation and the need for long-term clinical endpoint data. Confidence in the comparative rankings is moderate due to reliance on indirect evidence and potential bias from near-zero placebo events.

analysis.summary_en: This Bayesian network meta-analysis evaluated immunogenicity, efficacy, and safety of reduced-dose human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine schedules compared with the standard three-dose regimen. Using randomized controlled trial data from females aged 9–26 years, the study found that while three-dose schedules ranked highest for immunogenicity, single-dose schedules maintained clinically significant protection against persistent HPV infection with a superior safety profile. Two-dose schedules in adolescents aged 9–14 years appeared comparable to the three-dose regimen. The authors conclude that reduced-dose schedules can support global HPV immunization goals, particularly in resource-limited settings, though long-term clinical endpoint data are needed to confirm non-inferiority.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the potential role of high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs) in the pathogenesis of colorectal cancer, given the rising incidence rate of colorectal cancer in Iran and the suggestion that HPVs may contribute to its development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This preliminary study in South of Iran analyzed colorectal biopsy samples from 147 patients with colorectal cancer and 144 non-cancerous patients with colorectal inflammation and polyps to detect high-risk HPVs.
analysis.methods: The study used a nested PCR assay to test colorectal biopsy samples for the presence of high-risk HPVs, comparing results between cancer and non-cancerous patients.
analysis.main_results: High-risk HPVs were detected in 2 out of 128 colorectal cancer samples (1.56%, 95% CI: 0.48%-5.49%), while all non-cancerous colorectal samples were HPV negative.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as preliminary evidence that high-risk HPVs may be present in a small subset of colorectal cancer cases, but they emphasized that the study cannot determine a possible association between HPV infection and colorectal carcinogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that further research is needed to explore the potential role of HPV in colorectal cancer, which could inform region-specific screening strategies and HPV vaccination programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include its small sample size and the inability to establish a causal relationship between HPV infection and colorectal cancer, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This preliminary study in South of Iran investigated the potential role of high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs) in colorectal cancer. The study tested colorectal biopsy samples from 147 cancer patients and 144 non-cancerous patients using nested PCR. High-risk HPVs were detected in 1.56% of cancer samples, while none of the non-cancerous samples were positive. The authors noted that the study cannot determine an association between HPV and colorectal carcinogenesis. The findings highlight the need for further research to explore HPV's role in colorectal cancer, which could influence targeted prevention and management strategies. However, the study's small sample size and lack of definitive evidence limit its conclusions, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the scarcity of data on the vaginal microbiota (VM) in Madagascar and its interplay with prevalent urogenital infections, including human papillomavirus (HPV). The authors highlighted a geographic and social bias in existing VM research, which is largely derived from the Global North.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a cross-sectional characterization study of 443 adult women of reproductive age in the Marovoay District of Madagascar. The study aimed to describe VM variability in the presence of three urogenital tract conditions, including HPV infection.
analysis.methods: The VM was characterized by identifying community state types (CSTs) I–V, with CST IV (diverse) and CST III (Lactobacillus iners dominated) being the most prevalent. Alpha and beta diversity were assessed, and differential abundance analysis was performed to compare taxa among participants with HPV infection, female genital schistosomiasis, and controls.
analysis.main_results: CST IV was observed in 57.1% of participants and CST III in 34.1%. CSTs were associated with previous antibiotic usage, while alpha and beta diversity variability was linked to dietary behavior and prior antibiotic use. Differential abundance analysis revealed variations in specific taxa among HPV-positive participants compared to others.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as contributing to a broader understanding of vaginal health in Madagascar and addressing the research gap in sub-Saharan Africa by enriching microbiota databases. They emphasized the novelty of being the first study to characterize the VM in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future surveillance and research priorities in Madagascar by highlighting associations between VM composition, HPV infection, and other urogenital conditions. This could guide targeted interventions for women's reproductive health in the region.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference. The evidence strength is moderate due to potential confounding from dietary and antibiotic use factors and the lack of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized the vaginal microbiota (VM) of 443 Malagasy women of reproductive age in the Marovoay District, identifying CST IV (57.1%) and CST III (34.1%) as dominant community state types. CSTs were associated with prior antibiotic use, while VM diversity correlated with dietary behavior and antibiotic exposure. Differential abundance analysis showed specific taxa variations in HPV-positive participants. The authors interpret these findings as the first VM characterization in Madagascar, addressing a geographic research gap and contributing to broader vaginal health understanding. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and evidence strength is moderate due to confounding factors.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a major public-health burden in low- and middle-income countries with limited access to preventive services, and the distribution of oncogenic HPV genotypes in specific districts of Nepal was poorly documented.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A community-based, non-probability convenience sampling study collected cervical swabs from 2,331 women aged 20–45 years attending health camps in Rampur and Rambha municipalities of Palpa district between 7 February 2025 and 7 October 2025.
analysis.methods: Cervical swabs were processed for HPV DNA detection using a Nucleic Acid Extraction Kit and genotypes identified by RT-PCR with a Human Papillomavirus Nucleic Acid Amplification Test Kit.
analysis.main_results: HPV positivity was 3.5% among participants, with non-16/18 genotypes detected in 49.3% of HPV-positive cases, HPV 16 in 29.5% and HPV 18 in 16.9%. Women aged 35–40 years had the highest proportion of HPV-positive cases (36 cases).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the low overall HPV positivity and the predominance of non-16/18 genotypes as locally relevant for genotype-specific vaccination and screening strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform targeted HPV vaccination programs and genotype-informed screening algorithms in hilly districts of Nepal where genotype distribution data are scarce.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Convenience sampling and pre-analytical errors in 307 samples limit generalisability, and the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference; evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This community-based study in Palpa district, Nepal, assessed HPV prevalence and genotype distribution among 2,331 women aged 20–45 years attending health camps from February to October 2025. Using RT-PCR after nucleic acid extraction, HPV DNA was detected in 3.5% of participants, with non-16/18 genotypes comprising 49.3% of HPV-positive cases, HPV 16 in 29.5% and HPV 18 in 16.9%. The highest HPV positivity occurred in women aged 35–40 years (36 cases). The authors highlight the predominance of non-16/18 genotypes and low overall positivity as locally relevant for vaccination and screening strategies. These data can guide genotype-specific immunization programs and screening algorithms in hilly districts of Nepal where genotype distribution data are limited. However, convenience sampling, pre-analytical errors in 307 samples, and the cross-sectional design constrain generalisability and causal inference, yielding moderate-strength evidence.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Primary HPV screening detects premalignant and malignant cervical lesions with high sensitivity but low specificity, necessitating triage tests such as cytology. The study addresses the reliability of cytology in triaging hrHPV-positive women with negative or low-grade cytological findings and whether further evaluation can be safely deferred.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective hospital-based observational study was conducted on 125 women with a positive hrHPV cervical test. Participants underwent conventional cytology, extended HPV genotyping, colposcopy, and histopathological evaluation, with immunohistochemical analysis of p16 and Ki-67 expressions.
analysis.methods: Conventional cytology, extended HPV genotyping, colposcopy, and histopathological evaluation via biopsy or loop excision were performed. Immunohistochemical analysis of p16 and Ki-67 expressions was conducted on histopathological tissue samples, and associations between cytology, HPV genotype distribution, colposcopic findings, histopathology, smoking status, and biomarker expression were analyzed.
analysis.main_results: Among HPV-positive patients with NILM cytology, CIN2+ lesions were confirmed in 28.0% of cases. More than half (51.4%) of all CIN2+ lesions in HPV-positive women were identified in patients with low-grade or negative cytology. HPV16/18 positivity was prevalent among women with CIN2+ lesions and low-grade cytology (78.4%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets that deferring further evaluation of hrHPV-positive women based solely on negative cytology may be unsafe, particularly in older women, smokers, and those positive for HPV16/18. The strong association between p16/Ki-67 positivity and CIN2+ lesions suggests that dual-stain testing could improve triage strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against delaying evaluation in hrHPV-positive women with negative cytology, especially in high-risk subgroups, and support the use of p16/Ki-67 dual-stain testing to refine triage and reduce invasive procedures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-centre, hospital-based design and small sample size, which may affect generalisability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature and potential selection bias.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective hospital-based study evaluated 125 hrHPV-positive women to assess whether further evaluation could be safely deferred in those with negative or low-grade cytology. Among participants, 28.0% of women with NILM cytology had histopathologically confirmed CIN2+ lesions, and over half of all CIN2+ lesions in HPV-positive women occurred in those with low-grade or negative cytology. HPV16/18 was highly prevalent (78.4%) in women with CIN2+ lesions and low-grade cytology. Immunohistochemical markers p16 and Ki-67 showed high sensitivity (95.5%) and negative predictive value (93.3%) for detecting CIN2+ lesions in hrHPV-positive women with low-grade cytology. Smoking status was significantly associated with CIN2+ lesions (p < 0.001). The authors conclude that deferring evaluation based solely on negative cytology may be unsafe, particularly in older women, smokers, and HPV16/18-positive individuals, and propose dual-stain testing as a potential triage improvement.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection and a principal cause of cervical cancer, yet comprehensive and updated data on HPV prevalence and genotype distribution in Isfahan, central Iran, remain limited despite regional reports.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study analyzed HPV PCR and genotyping results from 4,973 women screened between 2015 and 2024 at a referral laboratory in Isfahan, central Iran.
analysis.methods: The study collected and analyzed HPV PCR and genotyping results alongside available demographic data from women referred for genital HPV screening.
analysis.main_results: Of 4,973 women screened, 819 (16.5%) tested HPV-positive, with HPV6 being the most common genotype (9.2%). Among HPV-positive women, high-risk types were slightly more frequent than low-risk types (55.2% vs. 44.8%), with HPV16 (14.4%) the most prevalent high-risk genotype, followed by HPV53 (13.2%) and HPV18 (6.2%). HPV positivity was highest in women under 20 years of age (27.3%; P = 0.002).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high HPV infection rate in Isfahan as comparable to other regions in Iran and noted that more than half of HPV-positive women were infected with high-risk types, highlighting the burden of oncogenic HPV in the population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a substantial burden of HPV infection and high-risk genotypes in Isfahan, which may inform local vaccination strategies and cervical cancer screening programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design and reliance on a single referral laboratory limit generalizability, and the absence of clinical outcomes or longitudinal follow-up reduces the strength of evidence for causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed HPV PCR and genotyping results from 4,973 women screened in Isfahan, Iran, between 2015 and 2024. Overall, 16.5% tested HPV-positive, with HPV6 as the most common genotype (9.2%). Among HPV-positive women, high-risk types predominated (55.2%), led by HPV16 (14.4%), HPV53 (13.2%), and HPV18 (6.2%). Infection was most frequent in women under 20 years (27.3%). The authors conclude that HPV prevalence in Isfahan is high and comparable to other Iranian regions, with a notable proportion of high-risk infections. These findings may guide local vaccination and screening policies, though the single-center, retrospective design and lack of outcome data limit generalizability and causal inference.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPV), particularly HPV16/18, is a principal driver of cervical carcinogenesis, yet the relationship between viral load and lesion severity across HPV subtypes remains incompletely defined. The study sought to quantify this association and to derive a clinical tool to guide triage of HPV-positive patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 331 high-risk HPV-positive patients whose data were collected between July 2025 and January 2026. Patients were stratified by HPV subtype (HPV16/18 versus 16 other high-risk types) and by cervical lesion severity into normal, LSIL, HSIL, and cervical cancer groups.
analysis.methods: Viral loads for HPV16/18 and the non-16/18 group were measured using a semi-quantitative hybrid capture–chemiluminescence platform. Multivariate logistic regression was used to assess associations among viral load, HPV subtype, age, and lesion severity, and a HSIL+ risk prediction nomogram was constructed and validated by bootstrap.
analysis.main_results: HPV16/18 infection prevalence increased with lesion severity (HSIL: OR=6.50; cervical cancer: OR=23.28), while non-16/18 viral load rose during LSIL and HSIL but declined in cancer. HPV16/18 types and medium-to-high viral loads were identified as independent risk factors for HSIL+, and the nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.763.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret HPV16/18 as the principal persistent driver of progression, whereas high non-16/18 viral load signals a critical precancerous window. They report a novel HSIL+ risk-stratification nomogram that integrates subtype-specific viral load and age for pragmatic clinical triage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support subtype-aware, viral-load–based triage to prioritize high-risk HPV-positive patients for early colposcopy or intervention, potentially reducing overtreatment and improving resource allocation in cervical cancer prevention programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design, single-center sampling, and reliance on semi-quantitative viral load measurement limit causal inference and generalizability; bootstrap validation yielded moderate discrimination (AUC 0.763), indicating moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study of 331 high-risk HPV-positive patients collected between July 2025 and January 2026 examined how viral loads of HPV16/18 and 16 other high-risk types correlate with cervical lesion severity. Using semi-quantitative hybrid capture–chemiluminescence assays and multivariate logistic regression, HPV16/18 infection showed a monotonic increase in prevalence with lesion severity (HSIL: OR=6.50; cancer: OR=23.28), whereas non-16/18 viral load peaked in LSIL/HSIL but fell in cancer. HPV16/18 and medium-to-high viral loads were independent HSIL+ risk factors, and a bootstrap-validated nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.763. The authors conclude that HPV16/18 acts as the principal persistent driver, while high non-16/18 viral load provides an early warning during precancer. They propose a pragmatic HSIL+ risk-stratification nomogram to guide triage and precision management.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) as the target pathogen and disease, focusing on therapeutic vaccines in preclinical models. The central question addresses the immunological and antitumor responses elicited by HPV-targeted therapeutic vaccines in HPV-associated HNSCC preclinical research.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review that synthesizes preclinical studies on HPV therapeutic vaccines, detailing vaccine components (antigens, delivery platforms, adjuvants, and combination agents) and assessing immunological and therapeutic effects in preclinical cancer models. The review explicitly frames its scope as describing current HPV vaccination strategies and their biological mechanisms in preclinical contexts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that HPV-associated HNSCC represents a significant disease burden, with HPV accounting for 22-70% of HNSCCs depending on the region. It emphasizes that therapeutic vaccines leverage viral tumor-specific antigens such as E6 and E7, which are easily targetable by immunotherapy in HPV-associated cancers. Additionally, the review notes the absence of FDA-approved therapeutic vaccines for HPV-associated cancers despite ongoing preclinical and clinical studies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a critical gap: while prophylactic HPV vaccines are effective against infection and oncogenesis, they are ineffective against established HPV infections and related cancers, leaving a therapeutic void. It also notes that standard treatments for HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancers (radiotherapy, surgery, and chemotherapy) can result in significant lifelong side effects, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic approaches.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the development and evaluation of therapeutic HPV vaccines, particularly in preclinical models, to address the lack of new treatments entering clinical practice over the past decade. It calls for continued research into vaccine components (antigens, delivery platforms, adjuvants) and their combinations to optimize immunological and therapeutic responses in HPV-associated cancers.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review focuses on human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and evaluates therapeutic HPV vaccines in preclinical models. HPV accounts for 22-70% of HNSCCs regionally, and while prophylactic vaccines prevent infection, they are ineffective against established cancers. Standard treatments for HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancers cause significant lifelong side effects, highlighting the need for novel therapies. Therapeutic vaccines targeting viral tumor-specific antigens like E6 and E7 show promise in preclinical studies, but no FDA-approved therapeutic vaccines exist for HPV-associated cancers. The review emphasizes the importance of optimizing vaccine components (antigens, delivery platforms, adjuvants) and combinations to enhance immunological and antitumor responses, calling for continued preclinical and clinical research to bridge the therapeutic gap.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines whether theory-informed educational interventions increase uptake of cervical cancer screening among underserved women, focusing on human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical cancer prevention and screening modalities such as Pap smear, VIA, or HPV testing.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis that searched seven databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and PsycINFO) for studies published between January 2005 and November 2025, identifying 1,200 records, screening 900 titles and abstracts, and assessing 200 full-text articles; 14 studies were included in qualitative synthesis and 12 trials contributed data for meta-analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Structured educational interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care or minimal information (pooled OR = 4.41; 95% CI: 2.21–8.80), with substantial effects observed in both high-income (OR = 3.46; 95% CI: 1.43–8.36) and middle-income settings (OR = 6.55; 95% CI: 2.74–15.63).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review did not report on the long-term sustainability of intervention effects, differential impacts across specific underserved subgroups, or the cost-effectiveness of theory-informed education programs.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Integrating theory-based educational interventions into national and local cervical cancer screening programs is recommended to reduce disparities in HPV-associated cervical cancer prevention, particularly in underserved populations.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether theory-informed educational interventions improve cervical cancer screening uptake among underserved women. Using a comprehensive search across seven databases from 2005 to 2025, 14 studies were synthesized qualitatively and 12 trials were included in a meta-analysis. Structured educational interventions significantly increased screening uptake (pooled OR = 4.41; 95% CI: 2.21–8.80), with notable effects in both high-income and middle-income settings. Interventions frequently incorporated behavioral frameworks such as the Health Belief Model and were often culturally tailored or community-embedded. The review concludes that integrating these interventions into screening programs could effectively reduce disparities in HPV-associated cervical cancer prevention.
